If $n > 1$: compute the scaling factor $s = 2 - \frac{1}{n}$, compute the normalized direction $u = \frac{p}{n}$, and return $p' = s \cdot u$ [S1].

The claim describes the computation for the case where $n > 1$ (which corresponds to $||p|| > 1$ in the source, assuming $n$ represents the norm $||p||$). The claim states: 1) $s = 2 - 1/n$, 2) $u = p/n$, 3) $p' = s * u$. Substituting these gives $p' = (2 - 1/||p||) * (p/||p||)$. This matches exactly with the formula provided in Source [S1] for the case $||p|| > 1$: $(2 - 1/||p||) * (p/||p||)$.
